title: Priority-based decode scheduler to reduce CPU-GPU handoff latency and threadpool contention
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Cut host-side overhead for short/interactive decode requests by 40-60% (absolute reduction target ~5-8ms per request) by implementing a priority-aware decode scheduler, tightening CPU-GPU handoff paths, and coordinating kernel selection heuristics with the scheduler. Background: We observe tail latency spikes and increased CPU/GPU sync events when small chat-like requests interleave with long prefills. Root causes include: threadpool contention in the decode workers, frequent small memcpy operations for KV cache handoff, and suboptimal kernel activation patterns that force repeated kernel launches for short sequences. Scope: scheduler changes, threadpool/work-stealing tuning, batched zero-copy handoff paths for short sequences, and a small set of kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused attention kernels for short decode bursts.
success_criteria: 1) Median host overhead for 0-64 token decode-only requests decreases by >=50% from baseline (baseline median 12.4ms -> target <=6ms). 2) P95 host overhead for mixed prefill+decode scenarios reduced by >=30%. 3) No regression (>1%) in token throughput for long streaming workloads. 4) Automated e2e perf test passes and release gating metrics green.
plan: 1) Prototype priority queue scheduler in the serving runtime (soft-priorities: interactive vs batch). 2) Introduce per-priority decode worker pools with limited core affinity to avoid cross-priority contention. 3) Implement a short-request fast-path that attempts zero-copy KV handoff and bypasses staging buffer when sequence length < 64 and model variant supports fused attention. 4) Add kernel selection hint API so scheduler can request low-latency fused kernels for priority==interactive. 5) Bench, iterate, and land opt-in feature flag behind runtime-1.19. 6) Canary rollout on dedicated pools and monitor cost/latency metrics for 72h before full release.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: - Per-priority pools increase memory footprint (extra worker stacks) but reduce mutex contention; acceptable given target deployments have headroom. - Zero-copy fast-path requires stronger invariants about KV ownership and alignment; will be gated behind model capability flags to avoid correctness risk. - Forcing fused kernels for short sequences may slightly increase per-token GPU compute for some models but reduces host-side latency; we limit this to interactive priority only. - Avoid global kernel cache invalidations; prefer local hints to kernel-selector to reduce cross-request interference.
milestones: - 2025-02-21: design review and kernel hint API spec accepted. - 2025-02-28: scheduler prototype + unit tests. - 2025-03-07: zero-copy fast-path implementation and microbenchmarks. - 2025-03-14: internal perf run and stability tests. - 2025-03-21: canary rollout start.
benchmarks_and_baseline: Baseline measurements from canary cluster on runtime-1.18: median host overhead (decode-only, 0-64 tokens) = 12.4ms, p95 = 37.1ms, GPU utilization per long-prefill job = 78%. Microbench: memcpy syscalls per short request = avg 3, threadpool wakeups = avg 9. Target improvements: median <=6ms, p95 <=26ms, memcpy syscalls <=1 on fast-path.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for scheduler invariants and priority demotion/escalation. - Integration tests with fake GPU backend to validate zero-copy semantics. - Synthetic load tests (short-only, long-only, mixed) in staging with token-level tracing turned on. - Regression harness against release branch measuring throughput and latency across model catalog (small/medium/large).
rollout_and_monitoring: Feature behind feature-flag (priority-decode-v1). Start with 10% canary on dedicated pools for non-production tenants, expand to 50% after 24h if no regressions, then full roll. Monitoring: per-priority median/p95 host overhead, memcpy syscall rate, threadpool queue depth, CPU steal time, and kernel-launch counts. Alerting rules added for >5% regression in throughput or >20% increase in error rates.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: zero-copy path may expose a rare race with KV cache eviction. Mitigation: conservative lock when enabling fast-path and add extra validation in dev stage. - Risk: fused-kernel preference could worsen GPU tail latency on some older cards. Mitigation: add hardware capability gating and canary on each GPU SKU. - Risk: increased memory footprint from extra pools may trip OOM in small dedicated nodes. Mitigation: auto-disable per-node when free-memory < 2GB.
open_questions: 1) How should we surface priority from API layer without exposing product-level semantics? Proposal: use internal routing hint header X-Redwood-Priority: interactive|background. 2) Do we want automatic demotion if user latency budgets are exceeded? 3) Should kernel-selector cache per-priority performance profiles?
